newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW resume talks to end parts plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW resume talks to end parts plant strike.

text.p: Bargainers sat down for more talks Friday morning to end a three-day old strike at a General Motors Corp. parts plant that is quickly rippling through the automaker's North American production operations.
Negotiators talked all day Thursday until breaking for the evening at 1:10 a.m. EDT Friday, said GM spokeswoman Darla Parks. They reopened talks at 9 a.m. Friday.

About 2,800 union members from UAW Local 909 walked off the job at the Warren, Mich., GM Powertrain Group plant at midnight Tuesday when talks failed to produce a new contract. The plant makes automatic transmissions for front-wheel drive vehicles, as well as wheels and suspension components.
A shortage of parts has forced GM to suspend production at a total of six car assembly operations with 16,900 hourly workers.

The other plants affected are in Lansing, Orion Township, and Flint, Mich. Those plants make the Buick LaSabre, Buick Riviera, Oldsmobile Aurora and Eighty Eight, Pontiac Grand Am and Bonneville, Oldsmobile Achieva and Chevrolet Cavalier.

In addition, an assembly complex in Oshawa, Ontario, that has two assembly lines shut down Friday morning. The facility produces the Chevrolet Lumina and Monte Carlo, and the Buick Regal and Century sedans.

GM and the UAW Local 909 are at odds over the automaker's desire to cut its total labour force and increase outsourcing of work. Union officials are demanding that GM add more employees to ease overtime burdens and address health and safety issues.
GM's stock fell 81.25 cents to $57.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
